articles.title: Panama Paradox
articles.angle: Offshore leaks are not just scandal archives but reusable infrastructure.
articles.technical_setup: Full ICIJ Offshore Leaks graph in Neo4j 5.16 with Cypher across entities, officers and intermediaries.
articles.methodology: Import all leak components, then compare leak sources, jurisdictions and intermediaries with a focus on repeated structural nodes.
articles.insight: Offshore is an organized network with a small number of switching points and a clear geographic division of labor.

reproduction_steps.name: Acquire the ICIJ graph input manually
reproduction_steps.summary: Place the public leak data export under data/manual_drop/icij_offshore_leaks/.

reproduction_steps.name: Load into Neo4j
reproduction_steps.summary: Map entities, officers and intermediaries to graph nodes and relationships.

reproduction_steps.name: Run structural queries
reproduction_steps.summary: Compare jurisdictions, intermediary concentration and leak-source overlap.

articles.title: Panama Paradox II: OpenSanctions x ICIJ
articles.angle: Historical leak data remains operationally useful inside current screening systems.
articles.technical_setup: ICIJ entity and officer exports plus OpenSanctions snapshot data and exact-name cross-matching.
articles.methodology: Use exact matches rather than fuzzy scoring, then split results into high-signal hits and manual-review candidates.
articles.insight: Historical offshore structures keep resurfacing inside sanctions, export-control and screening data.

reproduction_steps.name: Prepare leak and screening names
reproduction_steps.summary: Export comparable entity and officer name fields from ICIJ and OpenSanctions.

reproduction_steps.name: Run exact-match crossmatch
reproduction_steps.summary: Use a conservative exact-name strategy and store result counts by source and category.

reproduction_steps.name: Assess signal quality
reproduction_steps.summary: Separate high-signal hits from names that clearly require manual review.

articles.title: Die Weltkarte der Compliance-Schande
articles.angle: Country stories get sharper when multiple conflicting data layers are read together instead of through one index.
articles.technical_setup: A layered country view combining TI CPI 2025, FATF status, ICIJ leak exposure and World Bank debarments.
articles.methodology: Composite layering instead of one-dimensional country ranking.
articles.insight: No single index tells the full story; stronger enablers emerge only when multiple layers are overlaid.

reproduction_steps.name: Collect country-level inputs
reproduction_steps.summary: Gather CPI, FATF, World Bank and leak-linked country signals.

reproduction_steps.name: Normalize to one country table
reproduction_steps.summary: Align naming, date context and scale across heterogeneous sources.

reproduction_steps.name: Compare contradiction patterns
reproduction_steps.summary: Highlight countries that look clean on one layer but weak on another.

articles.title: Die Shell-Company-Fabrik
articles.angle: Shell-company abuse is best understood as registry design plus enforcement weakness, not as a single bad actor story.
articles.technical_setup: UK Companies House, ICIJ Offshore Leaks and NCA enforcement material in one registry-forensics frame.
articles.methodology: Read register design, shell-company signatures and offshore connections together.
articles.insight: The core problem is not openness itself but a registration model that long confused registration with verification.

reproduction_steps.name: Acquire the registry and context data
reproduction_steps.summary: Place Companies House and enforcement reference material under data/manual_drop/.

reproduction_steps.name: Build shell-company indicators
reproduction_steps.summary: Define address density, repeat directors, offshore links and enforcement context fields.

reproduction_steps.name: Rank structural enablers
reproduction_steps.summary: Focus on system-level weaknesses rather than one-off anecdotal cases.

articles.title: Follow the Bitcoin
articles.angle: Public blockchain visibility does not eliminate AML blind spots at scale.
articles.technical_setup: Elliptic Bitcoin data analyzed in Python with graph features, time windows and transition patterns.
articles.methodology: Study class distribution, hubs, illicit-to-licit transitions and the size of the unknown zone.
articles.insight: The bottleneck is not transaction visibility alone but the operational review layer around it.

reproduction_steps.name: Acquire the benchmark dataset manually
reproduction_steps.summary: Download the Elliptic dataset manually and place it under data/manual_drop/elliptic_bitcoin/.

reproduction_steps.name: Build graph features
reproduction_steps.summary: Load edges, features and labels into a simple Python analysis environment.

reproduction_steps.name: Measure the review gap
reproduction_steps.summary: Inspect illicit, licit and unknown transitions instead of just class counts.

articles.title: Anatomie Verdachtsmeldung
articles.angle: SAR pain sits between alert volumes, rare events and human review capacity.
articles.technical_setup: IBM IT-AML HI-Small analyzed in Python and Pandas with HTML/CSS/SVG presentation.
articles.methodology: Inspect transaction types, amount clusters, cross-border patterns, hub accounts and a simple alert-to-SAR funnel.
articles.insight: False positives are a math problem of rare events before they become an operations problem.

reproduction_steps.name: Estimate the SAR funnel
reproduction_steps.summary: Model how alert inflation erodes analyst capacity before escalation.
